Title: Mad, bad, and cap in hand! Help needed!

although it is work in progress, I can;t help thinking I'm missing
something.

David Hammond

i liked this deck when i saw it in action. If you are finding it to be
slightly "sticky" i suggest going for three disciplines instead of 4. i
would also double up on Enzo and Rudolpho and leave out Mario and
Francesca because you REALLY need NEC for this deck to work. Probably you
don't need the obf and pot skill cards which leaves two-three slots for
extra pool gain and/or power cards. The Succubus club could be good in
this deck - hire your loonies out for pool. There's maybe a case for
replacing some of the !Malks with malkavians and slipping in the Muddled
Vampire Hunter. Forgotten Labyrinth is probably a good addition to this
deck and if, as i suggest, you lose the potence then you might want to
build in some Disguised Weapon/Weapon combo action to replace it, and
Heidelberg Castle, too.


Messages.Author: skaffen_...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
In article <8sh8qm$946$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,
hamd...@my-deja.com wrote:
> Hello all,
>
> I played this deck last saturday at the Wedding of Anam and Ian, and
> although it is work in progress, I can;t help thinking I'm missing
> something.

I shouldn't really start talking about focus when such a bizarre idea builds
the foundation, but as you asked ;-)

Question: What is this deck going to do? It brings out Escaped Mental
Patients to go out and torporize vampires, then tries to resurrect the
lunatics via Necromancy. And it has to oust ist prey somehow. EMP need !Malk,
NEC Giovanni. For the part about ousting your prey that leaves you with two
generic strategies: bruise/bleed (Giovanni) or setalth/bleed (!Malk). What
you did is basically a standard Giovanni deck with some !Malks and EMPs:

>
> Crypt: (12 cards) [Min: 12, Max: 32, Avg: 5.00]
> 2 Carlotta Giovanni (Giovanni, 7, do NE ob
> PO)
> 1 Claven (Malkavian Antitribu, 4,
> au de ob)
> 1 Enzo Giovanni, Pentex Board of Directors (Giovanni, 8, an DO NE
> po th)
> 1 Francesca Giovanni (Giovanni, 4, do ne po)
> 2 Gloria Giovanni (Giovanni, 4, DO ne)
> 1 Mario Giovanni (Giovanni, 3, ne po)
> 1 Regina Giovanni, The Right Hand of Augustus (Giovanni, 10, au DO fo
> NE PO, 2 votes)
> 1 Rudolpho Giovanni (Giovanni, 3, NE)
> 2 Yorik (Malkavian Antitribu, 3,
> de ob)
>

Even for a Giovanni deck I find the average capacity of your vamps a bit,
err, intimidating. To get this looney parade going you need a !Malk and
someone with NEC as early as possible. Best bet for this are Rudolpho and
Yorik, but the odds are against this. Actually the odds are against having a
!Malk in your uncontrolled region at the start of the game reliably. I would
suggest going with the best vampires for Plan A (EMPs going, well, crazy) and
make Plan B (ousting your prey) according to the result. I would suggest more
smallish !Malks, an extra Rudolpho and Rafaele as well (obf/NEC at 6). Get
rid of Enzo and Regina – too expensive. The skills you use would be:
Necromancy, Obfuscate and one bleeder – either Dominate or Dementation (add
skill cards to get your choice on as many vampires as possible). Dominate
would let you steal the (hopefully) torporized victims of the EMPs with Grave
Robbing, so maybe that's the better (theme wise) choice.

What I find irritating is that your deck even has Plan C: intercept and D:
card retrieval through Carlotta and Whispers. I would think the whole setup
is complicated enough with just A and B. You have to recruit the EMPs,
resurrect them, maybe even clan impersonate to !Malk to start the whole
affair, and as soon as all opposing vampires are torporized get done with
your prey. That takes a lot of time and actions.

Please excuse what might read like harsh critizising and the lack of more
detailed suggestions (not enough time and resources at hand), I just got
carried away because I like to toy around with bizarre ideas myself as well
;-) And please post what sort of progress you are making.

Regards

Skaffen
Chantry Elder Of Munich

Shadows and shoals that edge eternity."

Thanks for this. I went home and had a think myself, and came up with a
few more ideas - especially along the lines of how to oust my prey.

I think I had been missing a way of stripping my preys resources, and I
had it under my nose all the time. More as we get there!

Yes, but you were missing that a significant portion of the deck was
the Dominate: Deflections (6 in my first attempt),dominate bleed
(which is also better than Dementation bleed as it is more flexible -
hence Govern the unalligned for the Superior to mitigate the pool cost
of influencing vampires).

My new approach goes...

As you can see, I have replaced the Sacrificial Lambs with Graverob,
giving me more scope to steal my prey "on the cheap" and use them to
hit my prey. By using agg damage, I get them (hopefully) full of blood.

Of course, this is full of holes (S:CE / Prevention!!!) but the idea is
I get (a maximum of) 15 shots - sooner or later a typical deck will run
out!!

I have also added a very small amount of Malkavian action in, just to
see if I can pull a Muddled Vampire Hunter. But also because of
Watendas useful ability!

Any more thoughts?

Aurora Van Brande is a Lasombra vampire with a relatively diverse
spread of disciplines (has OBT pot dom for). I think the concept
referred to here is that you tool Aurora up with a Camarilla Vitae

Recycling Aurora

12 copies of Aurora Van Brande as the crypt

some Camarilla Vitae Slaves
some Freak Drives
some Soul Gems
some Force of Wills
some Conditionings
some Daring the Dawns

Get Aurora into play. Get a CVS. Freak Drive.
Get a Soul Gem. Force of Will with Conditioning

the Soul Gem. Repeat until all 12 Auroras are

Carpe Noctem.

Actually, it involves tooling up with a Camarilla Vitae Slave and doing
nasty things involving costly blood cards and aggravated damage from
Daring the Dawn, along with a Soul Gem and, I think, Force of Will.

You spend so much blood that all the aggravated damages burns the
vampire. Camarilla Vitae Slave moves across with the Soul Gem power,
since it's a minion card, and allows you to do it again. And again. And
again.

Very vulnerable to bad card flow and bounce, but funny nonetheless.

Messages.Body:

> hamd...@my-deja.com wrote:
> > Incidentally, LSJ, If a Normal with discipline cards and the Soul Gem

>
> I don't think so, because when you use a Giovanni to bring back a burnt
> vampire, he doesn't remember what he'd done that turn, so the 'new'
> normal wont remember what old normal had done.

He would not, correct. The new normal doesn't have anything to do with the
old one - the amount of blood on the old one, the cards on the old one,
the actions of the old one - all are forgotten. The new Normal has a clean
slate.

> > And also, is a Golconda "removal from play" considered burning?
>

> dont know, kind of hope not, until i get a golconda anyway.

Removal from play is not burning.
